column1: # The benchmark cases of the optimizations: one row per case, its SQL in cases/ID.sql. `bench/bench cases` times each against PostgreSQL and the other engines;
# id: the case (bench/cases/ID.sql, the layout of bench/sql/store/queries: `--@ pg` the statement of every lane, `--@ sift` / `--@ duck` replace it, `--@ setup` DDL after the index)
# changelog: a phrase of the CHANGELOG line the case measures (the gate matches it; it must stay in CHANGELOG.md)
# dataset: orders (the store table of bench/sql/store/gen.sql with two derived columns, segment_id with 6,313 values and order_date)

# index: the columns of the sift_col index (`default`: every column of the store questions plus the derived ones; `default+title` adds the columns named after the +) and its WITH options; `-` for a case that makes its own tables
# plan: a regular expression the EXPLAIN of the sift lane must match (a load case: the output of its `--@ check`); a case that falls back to the normal plan fails
# baselines: engines besides sift and native (PostgreSQL with sift.enable_agg = off) that can answer it: pg_duckdb (the others: bench/engines.tsv, steps/store_engine.py)
# variants: name:SET a = b;SET c = d, further sift lanes with settings (the optimization turned off, or a lane without a pre-aggregate)
# metric: the number the README table shows: ms (warm median) or wal_bytes (per row)
# block: the generated block of README.md / docs/BENCHMARKS.md the case feeds (<!-- bench:NAME:begin -->)
# headline: yes puts the case in the README's table of application-shaped cases
